_comment: Phase 4. Payments that did not get authorised, as a share of payments that
reached a terminal state.
THIS ALERT REPLACED AN HTTP ERROR RATE THAT COULD NOT FIRE
The first version measured 5xx at payments-edge, which is the obvious thing
and is wrong. Measured during a chaos run with the provider failing 90% of
calls, the edge returned:
status=201  count=9,323
status=5xx  count=0
Every single one a 201, and correctly so. A declined payment is a business
outcome, not a transport error: the request was well formed, accepted and
processed, and the answer was no. Returning 5xx would tell the merchant's
own retry logic the failure was ours and worth retrying.
So an HTTP error rate on a payments API stays flat through a total provider
outage. It is a textbook alert on a series that cannot move.
UNKNOWN IS NOT COUNTED AS A FAILURE
F is FAILED/(all terminal states). UNKNOWN is deliberately excluded from the
numerator, because it is not a failure - it is a payment that may well have
been charged and whose fate nobody knows. Experiment 01 exists entirely to
reduce that state, and folding it into an error rate would make the deadline
budget's whole contribution invisible. It gets its own alert if it needs
one; it does not get to hide inside this one.
5% because the providers' own baselines are 0.1% to 4% declines, so a
threshold below 5 would fire on psp-b behaving exactly as configured.

annotations.description: More than 5% of payments reaching a terminal state were FAILED. UNKNOWN payments are excluded - those are a separate and more expensive problem, not a decline.
